title: A Summer for the Tide
premise: Dominic Okonkwo inherited a debt-ridden vineyard and an orchard deed bearing two names: his own and that of Ada Reyes, the woman who left him eleven years ago to build the career that saved her family. Neither can sell their half without the other, forcing them into a summer of uneasy partnership as developers circle and old betrayals resurface. When Dominic discovers Ada's employer is the developer trying to seize the orchard, loyalty and truth collide, and each must decide whether protecting their past selves matters more than the future they could share. They end the season by tearing up the sale, co-signing the orchard's survival, and boarding the last ferry together.
about_author: S. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former coastal-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing land disputes before turning them into love stories. They write from a converted ferry ticket office, where the tide schedule still dictates working hours.

chapters.title: The Deed with Two Names
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Buried in his late uncle's paperwork, Dominic finds the orchard deed listing both himself and Ada Reyes, the woman who vanished from his life a decade ago. A letter from a developer offers cash for 'the full parcel.' The beat is stunned disbelief — the past has arrived with legal standing.

chapters.title: Ada Comes Back for the Paperwork
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada arrives at the vineyard expecting a quick signature and an exit, but Dominic refuses to sign until he understands why her name is there at all. Their first conversation is all clipped professionalism over bad coffee. The beat is guarded friction masking unfinished grief.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Clearing storm-felled trees, they unearth a time capsule of letters and photographs from the summer they fell in love, revealing Ada's family once co-owned the land before selling out under pressure. The beat is bittersweet nostalgia softening old resentment.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada's boss, developer Marcus Hale, reveals she was sent to secure the orchard quietly — her career depends on closing the deal. She hides this from Dominic while accepting a deadline. The beat is complicity and dread; loyalty to her employer begins curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Forced to work the harvest together when hired labor falls through, they fall back into easy rhythm — arguments, laughter, one almost-kiss interrupted by a phone call Ada takes in private. The beat is warmth rekindling alongside the first real suspicion.

chapters.title: Invisible No Longer
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Town gossip links Ada to Hale's development project; Dominic confronts her, and she admits only half the truth — that she works for Hale, not that she was sent. He asks her to leave. The beat is heartbreak sharpened by the theme that staying invisible was always a choice.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Digging through the vineyard's true accounts, Dominic learns his uncle engineered the dual deed deliberately, betting the two of them would save each other — and the land. Meanwhile Ada drafts her resignation. The beat is revelation reframing everything as inheritance, not accident.

chapters.title: Hale Moves First
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hale, sensing delay, files a claim to force the sale and exposes Ada's original assignment to Dominic publicly at the town meeting. Humiliated and cornered, Ada chooses truth: she testifies against the project, torching her career. The beat is sacrifice as climax approaches.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the day the ferry makes its final autumn crossing, Hale's claim collapses on a technicality Ada risked everything to find. Dominic waits at the dock, unsure she'll come. She boards with one suitcase and no job. The beat is the climactic choice between what saved them and who sees them.

chapters.title: A Summer for the Tide
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Weeks later, they co-sign the restored deed, plant the first winter cover crop, and pin the old letters above the tasting room fireplace. Second chances, Dominic finally believes, are for people willing to be seen. The beat is quiet, earned resolution — the tide returns, and so do they.
